title: Moots County Line All-Road
content:
Moots just announced its County Line all-road bike, filling the space between its 50 mm Routt gravel bike and Vamoots road bike designed around a 38 mm tire…

Moots County Line Quick Hits

  • Frameset: $5,499
  • 1X or 2X Drivetrain Compatibility: A 45mm road chainline supports both 1x and 2x drivetrains, with clearance for up to a 50T 1x or 52/36T 2x setup.
  • Fully Integrated Front End: A new Moots carbon all-road fork uses a D-shaped steerer for internal brake routing through the Moots titanium stem.
  • All-Road Geometry: More stable than a traditional road platform, with size-specific 45mm and 52mm fork offsets to keep handling balanced across the full size range.
  • Built for Long-Day Rides: Fender mounts come standard, with optional upper rack mounts and room for a third bottle under the downtube.

Moots Drop-Bar Family

Gravel bikes have changed quickly. As tires got bigger and terrain got rougher, Moots’ dedicated gravel model, the Routt, moved with them. Today it’s built around a 50 mm tire, with room for considerably more. At the other end of the spectrum, the Vamoots remains what it has always been: a dedicated road bike.

38 mm All-Road Geometry

This new chassis is designed around a 38 mm tire, made for rides that move naturally between pavement and fast, well-maintained dirt roads. More tire, stability, and control than a traditional road bike, without the size, gearing, or off-road emphasis of a modern gravel bike.

County Line is designed to feel quick and responsive on pavement, with more stability and control than a traditional road bike when the surface gets loose. The 38 mm tire platform adds grip and comfort without the weight and volume of a modern gravel setup, while road gearing and relatively short 425 mm chainstays keep the bike efficient and lively under power.

County Line Pricing

  • Frameset $5,499.00
  • Force 1x $9,999.00
  • Force 2x $10,599.00
  • Red 1x $12,499.00
  • Red 2x $12,999.00
  • County Line RSL Framesets and builds coming in 2027
